outcome: maternal outcomes (morbidity, mortality, hospitalization, oxygen administration, obstetric complications, cesarean section rates)
neonatal outcomes (preterm delivery, low birth weight, NICU admission, mortality)
cohort: 471 pregnant women with confirmed COVID-19 infection who delivered between May 2020 and December 2021 in six hospitals in South India.
finding: Maternal morbidity and mortality (hospitalization for COVID-19 treatment, oxygen administration, and maternal deaths) were significantly higher in the second wave of the COVID-19 pandemic compared to the first wave, while obstetric complications, cesarean section rates, preterm delivery, low birth weight babies, and neonatal intensive care unit admissions did not differ between the waves.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were higher in women symptomatic with COVID-19 after 34 weeks of gestation.
